question: Irrespective of the source, pure water contains ______ of oxygen by mass.
solution:
The correct answer is 88.89%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A sample of pure water, whatever the source always contains 88.89% by mass of oxygen and 11.1%by mass of hydrogen.
 
• This is according to the law of constant composition.
 
 
• Water (H₂O) molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms of relative mass 1 and one oxygen atom of relative mass 16.
 
• Therefore, the ratio in which 2 atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen are combined is 1: 8.
 
 
 
• It will always be the same irrespective of the source of water.
 
• The total amount of percentage is 100, therefore they are divided in a constant ratio.
 
• As 2 atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen are divided in a ratio of 1:8.
 
• Therefore the mass of Oxygen in percentage terms in the compound is 88.89%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The chemical formula of water is H2O.
 
• Water contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• The molar mass of water, = 2×atomic mass of hydrogen + 1×atomic mass of oxygen.
 
• Therefore, the molar mass of water= 2×1+16=18g.
 
• Mass of oxygen in water: 16 g.
 
• Mass of hydrogen in water: 2 g.
 
• The formula for calculating the percent composition of any element in a given compound is:
 
 
• The mass percent of element = (Mass of that element in the compound/ Molar mass of compound)×100.
 
• So, mass % of hydrogen in H2O = (mass of hydrogen in H2O/Molar mass of H2O)×100
 
• = (2/18)×100
 
• =11.1%.
 
• Now, mass % of oxygen in H2O = (Mass of oxygen in H2O/Molar mass of H2O)×100
 
 

 =(16/18)×100

 =88.8%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Law of constant composition
 
 
• In a given compound, the elements always combine in the same proportion as each other.
 
• This implies that any pure sample of a compound, no matter the source, will always consist of the same elements present in the same ratio by mass.
 
• For example, pure water always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed mass ratio.
